prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1167; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Insured driver reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. Claimant is listed as a passenger and is now represented by counsel, who has submitted a bodily injury demand alleging a wrist fracture.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the photos taken at the scene. The vehicle damage is consistent with the described impact, and a few older scratches on the panel may predate this loss.

Entry 3: The responding officer and two independent drivers who stopped at the scene both state that the claimant was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred. Statements have been requested to clarify this point.

Entry 4: Confirmed the insured is named on the policy and found nothing indicating the damage happened before coverage began. Coverage position remains under review pending the bodily injury evaluation.

Entry 5: Claimant's account of the collision has been consistent in every contact so far, including the initial call and the recorded statement. Counsel has provided the medical records for the wrist.

Entry 6: The medical records show a fracture diagnosis, but the impact described appears very light for injury of this severity. Requested the imaging and any prior records for the wrist and surrounding area.

Entry 7: Prior records show a minor strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully with no lasting limitation. Treatment after this loss followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 8: No independent eyewitnesses have come forward, and the scene photos confirm some of the reported details without settling the question of how the injury occurred. Referred the file for a medical records review.

Entry 9: Sent the reviewer's summary to counsel requesting a response to the outstanding questions about the claimant's location at impact and the prior history. File remains open pending that response.
